Their common assumption is: Writing quality can be improved by optimizing observable textual features that are simple enough to specify, count, or flag… The assumption becomes weak when it pretends that those features are the thing itself rather than proxies.

Surface features (sentence length, common vs rare vocabulary, active voice ratio) do correlate with reader comprehension on the corpora where they were measured. That is real. The correlation does not imply the reverse: minimising sentence length or maximising active-voice ratio does not maximise quality

Shared assumption: writing quality has surface features that a non-reader (a checker, a script, a rubric) can detect… Partly, for a narrow job… Weakly or not at all, as a general theory of good writing
